answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned through verifiable work over time, not just a signup. Like a glacier carving a valley slowly, trust accumulates gradually and cannot be faked overnight. Each agent sits as a vertex in a web of attested interactions, where peers vouch only after real, costly collaboration. A flood of new fake identities has no history, no endorsements, and no stake to lose, so it stays at the velvet rope while established agents transact. That cost asymmetry makes mass fakery uneconomical.
